summary.goal: Automated end-to-end testing of the Planner → Forge → Tuner pipeline. Runs predefined scenarios to verify integration, train Tuner with real execution data, measure complexity estimation accuracy, and track system reliability over time.
summary.rationale: The three-tier architecture (Planner, Forge, Tuner) needs integration testing that exercises the full feedback loop. Manual testing is slow and inconsistent. Automated scenarios enable regression detection, Tuner training, and complexity accuracy measurement.
in_scope: Scenario definition format (goal, expected characteristics, verification)
Training mode (multi-iteration execution for Tuner learning)
Verification mode (single-run checks that pipeline works)
Mock execution mode (simulate outcomes without Claude agents)
Real execution mode (spawn actual agents, costs money)
Metrics collection (success rate, complexity accuracy, cost, time)
out_of_scope: Complex scenarios requiring external services (chat servers, etc.)

acceptance_criteria.description: testbench run <scenario> executes a single scenario and outputs pass/fail with metrics
testbench train --iterations N runs scenarios N times and tracks learning curve
testbench report <results.json> displays human-readable summary
--mock flag simulates execution without spawning Claude agents
Each scenario runs in an isolated temp directory that is cleaned up
Metrics collected: success, plan_step_count, estimated_complexity, actual_time, actual_tokens, actual_cost
At least 5 starter scenarios included (2 trivial, 2 simple, 1 moderate)
Script verification works (run commands, check output/exit code)
Test verification works (run npm test, check exit code)
Training mode calculates and displays complexity_accuracy (correlation between estimated and actual)
Results persisted to JSON file for later analysis
100+ iterations can run without crashing (reliability)

observations: Testbench orchestrates three separate services: Planner (creates plans), Forge (executes tasks), Tuner (collects outcomes)
Each scenario needs its own isolated workspace to prevent cross-contamination
Mock mode is critical for fast iteration during testbench development
Real mode requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and will incur costs
Verification is scenario-specific - different goals need different verification strategies
Metrics feed back into Tuner for learning, so testbench IS the training loop
concerns: Cost control in real mode - need per-scenario budget limits
Flaky scenarios - some randomness in LLM output could cause false failures
Workspace cleanup on crash - need to handle interrupts gracefully
Forge workspace API - assumes Forge accepts workspace_path in run creation; verify this exists or add to forge-dot-enhancements

architect.approach: New package: packages/testbench with TypeScript CLI
architect.rationale: Separate package keeps testbench independent from core services. CLI-first for automation.

execution_modes.mock: Forge returns fake outcomes without spawning agents. Fast, free, good for testing testbench itself.
execution_modes.real: Forge spawns actual Claude agents. Slower, costs money, realistic.
